1336:
** διηνεκής**,
_Doric dialect_ **διᾱνεκής** (see. below) {{Refs 1st c.AD+|“Supp.epigram” 1.327.10 (Callatis, 1st c.AD)}}, ές:— **continuous, unbroken,** ἀτραπιτοί τε διηνεκέες {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.195}}; νώτοισι.. διηνεκέεσσι with slices **cut the whole length** of the chine, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.321; ῥίζαι, ῥάβδοι, 12.134, 297}}; εἰ ὦλκα διηνεκέα προταμοίμην {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.375; so δ. σώματα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Hp.Ma.” 301b, compare 4th c.BC: Anaxandrides Comicus 6, “BGU” 646.22 (2nd c.AD)}}; ὄρος δ. {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 3.1.3; κανών “IG” 7.3073.108 (Lebad., 2nd c.BC)}}; τὸ δ. **regularity,** {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 2.355}}; of Time, **perpetual,** δ. νυκτί {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “VH” 1.19; δικτάτωρ εἰς τὸ δ. 2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Bella Civilia” 1.4.}} _adverb_ διηνεκέως in phrase δ. ἀγορεύειν to tell **from beginning to end,** {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.241, 12.56}} (**distinctly, positively,**{{Refs 8th c.BC+|4.836); ἅπαντα δ. κατέλεξε 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 627; compare τὰ ἕκαστα διηνεκὲς ἐξενέποντα 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 2.391}}; _Boeotian dialect_ and _Doric dialect_ διανεκῶς **without ceasing,** εὕδειν {{Refs 6th c.BC+|6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica 9 (uncertain), compare “SIG” 793.3 (Cos, 1st c.AD)}}; διηνεκῶς once in Trag., {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 319, “Comica Adespota” 382, 2nd c.AD: Marcus Antoninus Imperator 2.17, “OGI” 194.12 (Egypt, 1st c.BC), 1st-2nd c.AD: Dio Chrysostomus Sophista 49.8, etc.; so διηνεκές “hymnus ad Apollinem” 255, 3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Fragmenta” 158}}; also εἰς τὸ διηνεκές in **perpetuity,** {{NT+2nd c.AD+|NT.Heb.7.3, “PRyl.” 2.427 (2nd c.AD), “JHS” 33.338 (Macedonia, 2nd c.AD)}}; -κῶς **invariably,** opposed to πλεονάκις, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 18(2).315.}} — The _Aeolic dialect_ and _Doric dialect_ form διᾱνεκής is used also in _Attic dialect_, as {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Hp.Ma.” 301b, 301e (compare 4th-5th c.AD: Diogenianus Paroemiographus cited in Scholia (at [prev. work])), 4th c.BC: Anaxandrides Comicus [same place], “IG” 2.1054.81}}; but νόμος διηνεκής a **perpetual** law is read in {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 839a.}}
